# Unattended lifecycle regression tests — 13 September 2026  This follow-up uses fresh workspaces and one `Agent.runTurn` per trial. No game source is written by the supervising agent, and no follow-up repair prompts are sent into a trial. Independent checks run outside the generated workspace. A returned model answer is recorded separately from application acceptance.
## Final accepted results  Both selected builds completed unattended and passed a fresh repeat of the same **30-check gate**: fifteen groups in the real smolcoder preview and fifteen in a direct browser. This includes Play, visible terrain/HUD, mesh quality, gravity/jumping, WASD at three headings, visible mining/placement, repeated pause/resume, manual Save and reload, New World followed by visible editing, and malformed-save recovery. Screenshots were inspected separately. No manual source fixes or agent restarts were used within either accepted trial.
## Preview regression  Commit `1057acd` added iframe sandboxing without `allow-pointer-lock` or `allow-modals`. A first-person game could run directly but fail to leave its menu inside smolcoder. The previous browser test only exercised the direct URL and missed this regression.
## Matched ungated trials  The task is `bench/minecraft-lifecycle-prompt.txt`: a seeded voxel game with collision, editing, persistence, tests and a production build. Both backends use installed Qwen3.8 27B models labeled Q4_K_M, reasoning off, and a 32,768-token allocation. Their weight files have not been checked for byte identity. These are 27B-model tests, not evidence about 4B models or 8k windows. The providers run sequentially; the model loaded for a completed test is unloaded before switching providers.
## Changes under test  The first gated Ollama trial exposed a regression in `1057acd`'s write-payload eviction: it replaced old `write_file` arguments with a string describing omitted code. The model later copied that string into actual source files and spent many calls trying to recover. This trial was stopped and is not a passing result. The first fix turned completed large writes into plain assistant receipts and removed their paired tool results, preserving failed/pending calls and mixed batches. The final representation uses marked harness history records, as explained below. It never manufactures executable arguments. A narrow file-tool guard rejects the exact legacy marker without changing the file.
## Installed CLI and small-context follow-up  The user's global `smol` command was still using an older package. The tested checkout was packed and installed locally; all **35 compiled files** match the tested build byte for byte. The previous installation is backed up locally under `playground/.unattended/installed-backup/`. This does not publish an npm release.
## Reproduction  Install Playwright separately for the benchmark, or set `PLAYWRIGHT_PATH` to an existing installation. `CHROME_PATH` can name an installed Chrome executable. The harness itself has no new runtime dependency.
